summary: Khao kan chin (also called khao ngiao or chin som ngiao) is a Tai Yai/Shan-influenced northern Thai steamed rice parcel. For a practical Chiang Mai lead, Sanpakoi Kanomjeen at Thongkam Market currently lists it alongside noodles and northern dishes; stalls and availability can change.
whyGo: Taste a distinctive local rice preparation: cooked rice is seasoned, mixed with minced pork and a small amount of pig’s blood, wrapped in banana leaf and steamed.
The mild, savory parcel is commonly served with fried garlic, shallot and chilli, making it an easy small meal or snack.
Sanpakoi Kanomjeen offers a documented place to look: Michelin says its menu includes khao kan chin and places it inside Thongkam Market in Chang Moi.
bestFor: Travelers curious about Tai Yai/Shan and Lanna foodways, and pork eaters open to trying blood as an ingredient.
A casual lunch or snack paired with noodles or other market food.
skipIf: You avoid pork, blood products, or foods with uncertain ingredients; this dish is not vegetarian and should not be assumed halal.
You require a guaranteed blood-free, vegetarian, allergy-safe or fully documented menu; ask the vendor directly or choose another dish.
duration: Allow about 30–60 minutes for a meal stop; this is a planning estimate, not a published service duration.
cost: Michelin assigns Sanpakoi Kanomjeen the ฿ price tier and describes it as good value, but publishes no dish-level price. Carry small cash and confirm the current price before ordering; the amount may change by December 2026.
hours: Michelin currently lists Sanpakoi Kanomjeen as open Monday–Saturday 11:00–23:00 and closed Sunday. Individual market stalls and dish availability may differ; recheck close to your visit.
bestTime: Aim for lunch or early evening within the listed hours. Khao kan chin is also a portable lunch food, but the venue does not publish when this particular dish sells out.
gettingThere: The listed address is Thongkam Market, 11 Soi Thasatoi, Chang Moi, Chiang Mai. From the Old City, use a red songthaew, tuk-tuk or ride-hail; exact fares and journey times depend on pickup point and traffic. Confirm the market name/address with the driver.
booking: No booking is indicated for this street-food venue. Michelin lists cash-only service; bring Thai baht and check whether the stall is serving before making a special trip.
accessibility: Step-free access, seating, toilet provision and aisle width are not documented in the sources reviewed. Market access may involve uneven or crowded walkways; contact the venue or inspect on arrival if these details matter.
practicalTips: Show the name ข้าวกั๊นจิ๊น (khao kan chin) or ข้าวเงี้ยว (khao ngiao) when asking; names and spellings vary.
Ask whether it is available that day and say clearly if you have a pork, blood, fish-sauce or other dietary restriction. Ingredients and accompaniments can vary by recipe.
The rice parcel is mild; fried chilli and garlic are common accompaniments. Ask before adding chilli if you prefer less heat.
Sanpakoi Kanomjeen is known mainly for khanom chin with curries; consider khao kan chin one menu option rather than the venue’s sole specialty.
decemberNotes: No December-specific event or closure was found. The listed hours are current as of 17 October 2026 and are not a guarantee for December; check the Michelin listing or contact the venue nearer the trip, particularly around year-end holidays.
uncertainties: The cited restaurant listing confirms the dish is on the menu but gives no current portion price or day-by-day availability.
No venue-published accessibility details or December 2026 holiday schedule were found.
The Commons photograph is a representative 2013 image of the dish, not a photograph from Sanpakoi Kanomjeen.
